scope: New dir4 Bayer interpolation near unsupported green clipping; HL5, DR7, WB, matrices and supported formats unchanged. Legacy retained. D40 and postponed point 6 excluded; no language rewrite.
decision: Install the narrowly admitted colour correction. No measured regional regression versus frozen dir3 in these campaigns, but legacy still wins individual quality comparisons and all three current native D750 timing comparisons. No general superiority claim.
changes: The directional green interpolation can spread an unsupported clipped boundary into R/B colour differences. dir4 interpolates the observed two surfaces only at oblique/curved Bayer boundaries that already satisfy the common monotone mask and affine fits of the existing edge model.

Require original unreconstructed clipping only in green, entirely on the bright side, with a bit-exact green plateau. R/B must remain original measurements; the dark side must contain at least six measurements per channel spanning two CFA periods in both axes. Axial, multi-channel and R/B clipping retain the previous construction.

Only missing demosaic channels change. At this demosaic stage every supplied CFA sample remains exact, including the unreconstructed clipped plateau; HL5 recovery is unchanged and valid RAW measurements remain bit exact. No new inference of missing highlight hue, plateau lift, neutral assumption, RGB clamp or denoising.
Reuse existing support/provenance maps and bounded local stack storage; no additional frame allocation and no change to the memory plans.
Shared recipe/cache identity advances from dir3 to dir4. A cache regression rejects valid dir3/HL5 pixels. Worker metadata no longer embeds a stale HL4 label; the recipe is the version source.

v4_oblique_only.reason: D800 case with two clipped channels.

v7_spatial_dark_support.reason: Clipped-red case still failed colour checks.

rejected_variants.v8_selected_scope: Green-only is an empirical qualification boundary, not a theorem that arbitrary clipped boundaries are identifiable.

private_performance_trials.decision: Both rejected: no useful speed gain, the second slower in all three diagnostic files. Three repetitions plus one warmup are exploratory, not a final performance qualification. Neither changed production or the selected freeze.

fresh_verification.limits: 696 nonconstant new parameter realizations plus 112 ambiguity controls. RAW hashes are distinct from all development. 58 constant truth hashes recur in 68 control records. Phases, overlapping regions and noise pairs are correlated. Compatibility matrices generate and interpret truth; these are not calibrated camera measurements.

legacy_comparison.conditions: Identical source bytes, references, output geometry, WB and no exposure fit within each quality pair. One decode per engine for these small quality cases, not a timing benchmark.
legacy_comparison.limits: Counts refer to regional metric comparisons, not independent scenes. Overlapping regions and CFA phases correlated. Known-model matrices also generate truth. Chroma can be unbounded for signed RGB with small sum; no DeltaE. No general superiority or physical camera calibration claim.

photographic_checks.limits: Reused photographs and derived DNGs are not independent camera truth. Surrogate RGB is treated as linear Rec.2020 for the model; source camera/transfer/gamut error is not calibrated away. No measured photographic, noise or physical colour improvement claimed.

timing.order: Alternates within each source and across source index.
timing.scope: Decode-only timing includes broker input hash, XPC and transfer, excludes output hash, image analysis and disk reports. Warm OS caches; no whole-machine RSS, cold-start or physical camera accuracy claim.
timing.limits: Native complete pipelines have different crops: autonomous 6016x4016, legacy 6032x4032. These are the same source bytes, not equal output work. All output hashes repeat. No concurrent test/build/GUI campaign; ordinary OS activity and temperature uncontrolled. No cold-start or memory-pressure qualification.
timing.result: Autonomous is slower in all three measured files. The colour correction is retained; no lower-quality fast path was introduced to win the timing comparison.

open: Legacy retains local quality advantages on rejected coloured boundaries, texture and fully clipped fields; complete clipping can represent different hues or detail with identical RAW codes.
The selected dir4 scope does not extend to red/blue clipping, multiple clipped channels or axial/insufficiently supported boundaries. Broader variants failed local colour or gradient checks.
The new native D750 timing comparison favours legacy by about 3-19%; further exact implementation optimization remains open.
Ten previously tracked peak comparisons on seven signals remain worse than HL2, unchanged by dir4. This is a follow-up, not a new exhaustive HL2 comparison.

Measured profiles, physical targets/illuminants and sensor clipping plateaus; broader independent photographic evaluation; adequate X-T5 registration; memory pressure and global sandbox/release gates remain open.
